title: Functions Take Ownership
story: You give a gift to a friend — it's theirs now. In XIOM, passing a value to a function is like giving a gift — the function now owns it.
why: Functions taking ownership enables zero-cost abstractions — the compiler knows exactly when to free memory without a garbage collector.
analogy: Passing a value to a function is like giving a gift — once you hand it over, it belongs to the recipient. You can't use a gift you already gave away.
try_it: Try adding `io.println(my_vec.len());` after the call to `print_and_drop`. See the compiler error about using a moved value.
tips: A function signature without & means 'I take ownership'
Functions that own values automatically free them at end of scope
Returning a value from a function also transfers ownership to the caller
Use owned parameters when the function should decide the value's lifetime
common_mistakes: Forgetting that passing without & moves ownership — use & to borrow instead
Trying to use the same value in multiple function calls without cloning
Confusing 'taking ownership' with 'modifying' — you can take ownership of an immutable value
